segments.text: [style: brisk, clear, architectural voice; steady studio cadence] Book Four, Proposition Five. About a given triangle to circumscribe a circle. Let A B C be the given triangle; it is required to circumscribe a circle about the triangle A B C.

subsegments.text: [style: brisk, clear, architectural voice; steady studio cadence] Book Four, Proposition Five. About a given triangle to circumscribe a circle. Let A B C be the given triangle; it is required to circumscribe a circle about the triangle A B C.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: [style: methodical, precise constructive cadence] Bisect the sides A B and A C at the points D and E by One Ten, and from D and E draw D F and E F at right angles to A B and A C. They will meet either within the triangle A B C, or on the line B C, or outside B C. Join F A, F B, and F C.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: [style: luminous, deductive geometric clarity] Because A D equals D B, and D F is common and at right angles, by Side-Angle-Side congruence the base A F equals F B. By the exact same reasoning on side A C, C F also equals A F, so the three segments F A, F B, and F C are all equal to one another. Therefore the circle described with center F and radius F A passes through A, B, and C, and is circumscribed about the triangle A B C—with angle B A C acute when F falls inside, right when F lies on B C, and obtuse when F falls outside. Which was to be done.

segments.text: [style: reflective, scholarly, architectural synthesis] Proposition Four Five establishes the circumcenter of any triangle as the intersection of two perpendicular bisectors, unifying all three cases—acute, right, and obtuse—under Thales' semicircle theorem, Three Thirty-One. As Simson and Todhunter observed, the perpendicular bisectors of two non-collinear sides must always meet because lines perpendicular to intersecting lines cannot be parallel. In the GEOMETOR G-Index, node G one hundred fifty-seven synthesizes fourteen direct prerequisites across fifty-one ancestor nodes, directly powering the regular pentagon and golden triangle constructions of Propositions Four Ten, Eleven, and Twelve.
